qti-assessment-test.title: CIAO Seminars - Modified Barium Swallow Interpretation & VitalStim NMES Safety (ASHA / AOTA CEU Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Correlate pyriform sinus residue and reduced UES opening on MBS with targeted biomechanical rehab.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Correlate pyriform sinus residue and reduced UES opening on MBS with targeted biomechanical rehab.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: On lateral Modified Barium Swallow (MBS) imaging with thin and mildly thick barium, a post-stroke patient demonstrates reduced anterior-superior hyolaryngeal excursion, incomplete upper esophageal sphincter (UES) traction opening, and post-swallow pyriform sinus residue leading to post-swallow aspiration (PAS 8). Which physiological intervention directly targets the primary impairment?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Implement Mendelsohn maneuver and Shaker/CTAR suprahyoid strengthening trials (after verifying compensatory chin-tuck/head-turn response under fluoroscopy) to increase hyolaryngeal traction on the UES.
Prescribe labial seal and buccal tension exercises exclusively to eliminate pyriform sinus pooling.
Clear the patient for regular thin liquids at bedside because no audible cough occurred during the MBS exam.
Diagnose primary lower esophageal sphincter achalasia from lateral cervical fluoroscopy alone without esophageal screening.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Reduced anterior-superior hyolaryngeal excursion impairs mechanical traction opening of the cricopharyngeus/UES, causing pyriform sinus residue that responds to Mendelsohn and suprahyoid exercises.
Incorrect. Labial and buccal exercises address anterior oral spillage and sulci pocketing, not pharyngeal hyolaryngeal traction or UES opening.
Incorrect. PAS 8 indicates silent aspiration below the true vocal folds without a protective cough reflex, making bedside cough absence clinically deceptive.
Incorrect. Pyriform sinus retention reflects pharyngeal/UES mechanics, and distal esophageal motility disorders require dedicated esophageal/manometric evaluation.

qti-assessment-item.title: Identify absolute precautions and contraindications prior to anterior cervical dysphagia NMES.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Identify absolute precautions and contraindications prior to anterior cervical dysphagia NMES.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: An inpatient SLP/OT dysphagia clinician is evaluating a 74-year-old patient with severe pharyngeal dysphagia for VitalStim neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES). Which medical history finding represents a critical precaution/contraindication against placing active NMES electrodes over the anterior neck?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Presence of an implanted demand cardiac pacemaker/automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (AICD) or electrode placement directly over the carotid sinus.
Mildly reduced tongue-base retraction documented on videofluoroscopy two days prior.
Use of IDDSI Level 2 mildly thick liquids during supervised therapeutic bolus trials.
Intact cognitive-communicative alertness allowing the patient to report sensory tingling vs. motor grab thresholds.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Electrical current across the anterior neck risks electromagnetic interference with demand cardiac devices and baroreceptor-mediated bradycardia/hypotension if placed over the carotid sinus.
Incorrect. Reduced pharyngeal/suprahyoid biomechanics confirmed via instrumental assessment is an appropriate clinical target when paired with active swallowing exercise.
Incorrect. Combining instrumentally safe IDDSI bolus trials with active swallowing during NMES supports task-specific neuroplasticity.
Incorrect. Reliable patient feedback facilitates safe amplitude titration from sensory tingling to motor recruitment.

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply neuroplastic task-specificity principles during NMES-assisted dysphagia therapy.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Apply neuroplastic task-specificity principles during NMES-assisted dysphagia therapy.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Why do evidence-based dysphagia rehabilitation protocols pair motor-level NMES stimulation with simultaneous volitional swallowing tasks (e.g., Effortful Swallow on safe bolus trials) rather than applying passive electrical stimulation while the patient rests quietly?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Experience-dependent neuroplasticity ('specificity' and 'use it and improve it') requires cortical swallow-network drive synchronized with peripheral Type II/Type I muscle recruitment, and passive hyoid depression at rest without volitional elevation can work against airway protection.
Passive stimulation at rest permanently denervates cranial nerve XII motor nuclei within a single 30-minute session.
ASHA CEU billing rules prohibit recording session minutes unless at least 40 bolus swallows occur per minute.
Surface NMES selectively stimulates smooth muscle peristalsis in the distal thoracic esophagus during quiet rest.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Pairing volitional swallowing effort against NMES resistance drives central-peripheral swallow reorganization and trains functional hyolaryngeal elevation.
Incorrect. Passive NMES does not denervate hypoglossal nuclei; its limitation is lack of task-specific central swallow patterning.
Incorrect. Swallow repetition targets are governed by patient fatigue, respiratory coordination, and motor-learning pacing rather than an arbitrary 40-per-minute quota.
Incorrect. Anterior cervical surface NMES recruits striated pharyngeal/extrinsic laryngeal muscles, not distal thoracic smooth muscle.
